question: to the Commission Eleonora Meleti (PPE) Subject:

The increasing provision of specialised and complex medical procedures in private outpatient healthcare units raises important questions regarding the suitability and licensing of facilities, compliance with health standards and the professional qualifications, specialised education and continuous training of healthcare professionals. Ensuring that these procedures are carried out by adequately trained personnel, in appropriately licensed and equipped facilities, is a key prerequisite for the quality of services and patient protection. In the context of the free movement of professionals, mutual recognition of professional qualifications and lifelong learning, it is important to examine the extent to which the European framework responds to new requirements for specialisation and developments in the healthcare sector. In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission consider that the current European framework is sufficient to ensure that complex medical procedures are performed in appropriately licensed and equipped facilities by healthcare professionals with the requisite qualifications, specialised training and clinical experience?

Does the Commission intend to examine, alongside Member States, the need to strengthen European guidelines and exchange of best practices on the supervision of private healthcare providers, the licensing of specialised medical procedures and the continuing professional training of healthcare professionals?
